newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom plans 1997 Eurobond issue, sees delay.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom plans 1997 Eurobond issue, sees delay.

text.p: Russian telecommunications company Rostelekom RTKM.RTS plans to launch a Eurobond in 1997 but it will take some time for all details to be settled, a top financial official for the company said on Monday.
"We are still at the first stage of issuing Eurobonds," said Mikhail Kulakov, assistant head of the shareholder relations department for Rostelekom.
He said Rostelekom was in talks with Merrill Lynch on the issue, but he gave no details.

He said Rostelekom's planned issue of level one American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) was being held up. "According to the most optimistic predictions, (the issue will be resolved) in about three months", he said.
Kulakov also confirmed that Rostelekom planned to issue level three ADRs.
"Discussions on this are happening, but for now they are only discussions...We only have international-standard financial accounts dating back two and a half years," he said.
Coopers & Lybrand is conducting a financial audit of Rostelekom.
The Russian government is Rostelekom's main shareholder, with 51 percent of the company's voting shares, which is to be transferred to domestic telecoms holding company AO Svyazinvest.
Foreign investors own 30 percent of Rostelekom's ordinary shares and 50 percent of the prefered shares.
At 1520 GMT on Monday Rostelekom had ticked down to $3.305 from Friday's close of $3.310.
